extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: IFEval is a benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using a set of 'verifiable instructions' such as 'write in more than 400 words'. It consists of 25 types of verifiable instructions and around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions that can be automatically and objectively verified.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a combination of few-shot prompting and manual human curation. The process involved four steps: generating base prompts with randomly selected verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, rephrasing prompts to increase diversity, and manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 541 prompts containing 25 types of verifiable instructions, generated via few-shot prompting and manual curation. Model responses were collected from GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small via API calls.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 responses collected in November 2023; PaLM 2 S responses collected in August 2023.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human evaluation methods can introduce biases and inconsistencies; IFEval aims to be unbiased by using verifiable, automatically checkable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% objectively and automatically verifiable; edge cases exist where compliance is hard to determine (e.g., markdown formatting variations). Current implementation lacks diversity in verifiable instructions and does not support multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Ensuring LLMs can consistently follow instructions is important for safety and reliability, particularly in high-stakes domains like healthcare or autonomous systems where misunderstandings can have serious consequences.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models; comparing different LLMs on various instruction types; identifying which types of instructions are not usually followed.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and prompts are released on GitHub; future work plans to improve prompts, expand verifiable instructions, and add multi-modal support.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts are generated through few-shot prompting to remove illogical prompts, rephrasing for diversity, and manual curation
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Base prompts are filtered for logical consistency via few-shot prompting, then rephrased for diversity, and manually reviewed and edited

name.evidence: we introduce Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval) for large language models.

description.evidence: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark. It focuses on a set of 'verifiable instructions' such as 'write in more than 400 words' and 'mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times'. We identified 25 types of those verifiable instructions and constructed around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.

isLiveDataset.evidence: we create a list of 25 verifiable instructions. We further create a set of 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or multiple verifiable instructions.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We alleviate these problems by creating our prompts through four steps. First, we generate a set of base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Then, we use few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts and remove them. As the third step, we apply another few-shot prompting based approach to rephrase each prompt, to increase the diversity of phrasing. Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Human evaluation... is time consuming, expensive and relies on a set of human annotators, leading to potential biases and inconsistencies for reproducibility.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: it is important to note that while we focus on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically – there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
